summary: The ARIA runner habitat cannot be applied: its interactive-slice budget (user-.slice MemoryMax=3G) is sized for a retired 7.8 GiB droplet while the host has 31 GiB and the operator's sessions hold ~11 GB, and provision_runner.sh apply also installs and enables aria-gateway + telemetry, so the drift gate never passes and the runner ran without limits

A plan converged in a cycle whose profile lacks pr_create is stranded: implementation runs only on the same cycle's converged verdict, CONVERGED is terminal, resume skips terminal plans and no verb implements an existing converged plan

Plan synthesizer sources: the ORPHAN heading pattern matches no current orphan-findings.md heading, GitHub issue candidates are never converted, and F-findings rank newest-first against the documented oldest-first order

messaging-service's similar-message search asks request.ai.generateEmbeddings for the query vector, but no service answers that subject, so the pgvector search over messages.embedding cannot return a result; it also contradicts the owner decision that message history is not a raw retrieval corpus

Typed-judgment Phase 7 (the System-1 reflex layer: provider jev via tools/aria-poc/jev_runtime.py and the question bank aria_kernel/system_one_questions.py) is designed but not built on main or any branch, and ARIA's semantic memory has no embedder configured anywhere

The state snapshot detects a surface change between its two passes only by (dev, inode, mode, mtime_ns, ctime_ns), so a same-size rewrite inside one filesystem timestamp tick is invisible; test_root_inode_stability_does_not_hide_child_content_mutation fails intermittently on main and on PRs

The ack ledger's HMAC key lives under <tools>/secrets inside the aria/state store worktree, which is never published and is swept by the self-hosted lanes' git clean -ffdx at job start, so an operator-minted ack token cannot verify in any later runner job

The failing_ci plan source treats every red workflow on main as a verdict about main, so observer and post-deploy workflows (and workflows whose verdict is about a pull request) outrank ARIA's own findings; no manifest declares which workflows judge main

The F_FINDING plan source (priority 3) turns ARIA's own findings into grounded plans with no operator act, and none of ADR-0003's self-feed loop guards exist: no originating-skill self-loop filter, no per-24h cap on ARIA-emitted findings reaching the planner, no cycle detection over recently resolved findings

A converged plan's revisions can widen affected_surfaces beyond the grounding the request or F finding was admitted on, and the implementation write scope is the converged plan's surfaces minus READONLY_PATHS, so the admitted grounding does not bound what the implementer may write

ARIA forgets what it learned every week: state compaction keeps memory/learning-events only inside --retain-days (7) and collapses memory/beliefs, archiving the rest where no memory reader looks, so the live memory held 8 beliefs and 33 learning events on 2026-10-02 against 8 MB of archived history each
A rolled-back aria/state can re-admit a spent operator request inside its signed window (up to 168h): the merge lane's merged-once proof reads the same ledgers a rollback erases

Check 12 confirms an operator request's signed terms and that a grounding digest is present, but never compares the signed finding_id and grounding_digest with the plan_started content of the plan it merges

The operator signs an opaque digest: the recorder prints the canonical subject, whose grounding is a sha256, not the refs and writable surfaces the request will authorize, and nothing refuses to sign as root from a checkout or cwd another user can write
docs/aria/policy/ is not in implementation_safety.READONLY_PATHS, yet operators.json there sets the operator request lifetime and audience that ingestion reads from the working tree

Operator request ingestion verifies every historical request row with ssh-keygen before the spent check and re-lists every spent request in each scan row, so plan-source time and the ingestion ledger grow with history
The ingestion trust anchor rests on the runner-writable local refs/remotes/origin/main and re-hashes only the allowed-signers blob, not the commit or tree that names it

shared.access_logs keeps full request paths with query strings and, outside the hash-gated regions, raw client IPs (2.48M rows since 2026-07-12); nginx writes the combined format with IPs and query strings
Prometheus runs with 15-day retention and without the 127.0.0.1:9090 binding its compose file declares
The GraphQL codegen workflow never sees operations outside src/graphql and diffs only aquamobil and shared-ui output, so drift in module hooks (farm hooks/use*.ts) is never regenerated or checked
The leave list's status filter sends lowercase literals cast to LeaveRequestStatus, while the GraphQL enum's wire keys are uppercase, and it omits draft and withdrawn, so filtering by status fails

Runtime signals are lost or merged: the bridge overwrites one JSON file per signal on resolve, every runtime pressure gets the same id pressure:runtime_signal:unknown, and the hourly watchdog ingests into a throwaway checkout
The npm security audit runs on a PR only when package files change and stops at the first failing scope, so new advisories turn main red with no code change and three of six scopes go unchecked
The public aria/state branch publishes ARIA's raw LLM prompts and responses (tools/agent-invocations prompts 16 MiB, outputs 33 MiB), and a public Actions artifact carries the whole tools tree
Operator signatures cannot distinguish the operator from a root agent session on the host: the ed25519 operator key is root 0600 without an interactive passphrase and is also the commit-signing key
Event-bus delivery metrics are never scraped: event_bus_handler_outcome_total and event_bus_dead_letter_total live on prom-client's global registry, which /metrics does not serve
No deploy sets RELEASE_VERSION, so error groups never record the release they appeared in, and the farm service runs an image tagged farmsetup-fix-13 instead of a commit SHA
GraphQL errors and request-validation rejections are invisible per operation: the gateway has no error plugin, production masks errors, and whitelist rejections are logged without route or DTO
The label queue is not blind and records no sampling design: each item shows the AI judges' verdicts, quotas split evenly across strata, no inclusion probability is kept, and verdicts are binary

The registry single-writer runbook's Flip 2 cannot be applied: merge queue rulesets are not available on a user-owned repository, and the runbook's merge_method 'merge' contradicts the kernel's squash requirement

Every merged fix PR turns main's test job red until a separate reconcile PR lands: the closure-drift spec checks origin/main, and since 2026-08-31 a deploy needs the same run's test to be green, so only reconcile merges are deployable
The self-hosted runner works at its memory ceiling: the runner cgroup peaked at 2.41 GB against MemoryHigh 2.3G with 11,383 memory.high events
The dead-contract scan sees only `export const UPPER = ...` operation definitions and keys them by constant name, so 81 operation names defined in more than one file collapse into one
Self-hosted lanes starve each other: the hourly watchdog fired only 3-7 times a day, and the shared concurrency group keeps one pending slot, so a new job cancels a pending cycle

The genesis ladder's EVAL_WINDOW and ACTIVE rungs have no writer: the only production recorder stops at SHADOW, so the superiority-gated promotion the ladder exists for is unreachable, and the surface-reachability waiver for both expires on 2026-10-16 citing ORPHAN-HIGH-689, an id neither store holds

JetStream durable consumers hold no services.yaml subscribe grant naming the event they consume, so the plan-coverage witness's event-consumer closure, built from those ACL grants, sees 6 of 50 known consumer pairs and misses 44 across 8 services (e.g. notification-service's UserInvited handler)

tools/ripple-tracer/cli.ts still parses services.yaml with a quoted-only list-item regex, matches against the abandoned AQUACULTURE_EVENTS.<T>.> subject and never reads application:, so it reports no producers and no subscribers for any event while the change-event-contract skill treats its output as the authoritative consumer set

braces GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm stays reachable in dev and build tooling with no non-breaking remediation (graphql-codegen and its loaders, tsc-alias, the nx dev-server proxy, tailwindcss 3, the e2e jest 29 tree) and is held by a reviewed exception that expires 2026-11-03
messaging-service knowledge-extraction and retention-policy pin search_path with the search_path-only helpers; whether each callsite already holds a tenant RLS context is unverified
83 @InputType fields in farm-service, hr-service and auth-service carry no class-validator decorator; a mutation that sends them is rejected by the global forbidNonWhitelisted pipe
sensor-service passes its source schema to the tenant boundaries as hand-written 'sensor' literals and four file-local SENSOR_SCHEMA constants instead of one constant

emit_finding appends the finding_emitted event before it checks that F-NNN.json is free, so a file the ledger never emitted (F-101/F-102 on the runner store, legacy seeder output) turns the mint at that id into a phantom event and every later mint re-allocates the same id; reflection, the F_FINDING plan source and the watchdog FP harness glob F-*.json instead of reading the event fold

vitest 3 and its tinypool carry critical advisories (tinypool prototype-pollution RCE gadgets, @vitest/mocker path traversal) with no patch on vitest 3; dev-only, excepted until the web modules move to vitest 4
tailwind 3 in the root and AquaMobil trees pulls postcss-selector-parser 6.x, quadratic on crafted selectors (GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf); build-time only, excepted until both move to tailwind 4

A sensor's siteId is only format-checked: registration never asks farm whether the site exists, belongs to the tenant and is live, so a sensor can point at a deleted or foreign site and inherit the wrong zone and location
farm.tenant_localization is projected from TenantUpdated only when localization changes, with no backfill from auth, and tenant erasure leaves its row behind
The readings page's warning and critical counters count each channel's last value from up to seven days back, so a probe that alarmed last week and then went quiet still counts as a current warning

Manual-measurement and channel-editor units still live outside the measured-quantity registry: the farm measurement entity documents hydrogen_sulfide in mg/L while the engine and templates use ug/L, the farm history table and the channel editor keep their own unit lists

The admin OpenAPI generator writes union members in the TypeScript checker's internal type-id order, so adding string literals anywhere in the program reorders enums in unrelated DTOs and turns the artifact gate red on a PR that changed no admin contract

Copies of the measured-quantity vocabulary remain outside the registry and contradict it: frontend unit and alias tables (water level shown in m and alarmed in % while channels store cm), the water-chemistry mock's units, a second reading-range table in sensor data quality, and a second reading-field map in the gateway

The flat SensorReading event projects a channel by its key alone, so a declared quantity is ignored there: a `do` channel declared as % saturation is still published as dissolved oxygen, and child sensors registered before the catalog fix keep their AMMONIA type and publish TAN as `ammonia`

The e2e NATS RPC scan reads a responder's `.respond(SUBJECT` as a send, so request/reply contracts are left out of it and farm-service holds a publish grant on its own handled subject request.farm.validateSiteAssignment
Water-quality answers to the AI assistant name a measurement's unit only through tankId, so a measurement taken at non-tank water equipment (biofilter, sump) reaches the assistant with no unit
The water-chemistry history table names a measurement's unit from tankId only, so rows filed at water equipment (and tank rows from the old batch form) show '-'

System-level water-quality readers take a system's units from tanks.systemId only, so equipment-table tanks and equipment linked through equipment_systems are left out of a system's chart, statistics and list

Three judge/verification mint paths outside the pressure lane still put non-repo refs into evidence_refs (cycle:<id>, plan:<id>, and self-output beside a repo ref), so create_agent_invocation_request cannot yet refuse the ARIA-HIGH-384 class for every role

A sensor that publishes MQTT directly has no broker identity: field devices are handed the sensor_service account, which can read and write every tenant's sensor, device, alert and command topics, and a free-text topic resolved first-match across tenants lets one tenant capture another's stream

The MQTT auth endpoints' shared secret is never transported: mosquitto-go-auth (3.0.0, latest) has no custom-header option, so auth_opt_http_headers X-Mosquitto-Auth is inert and /mqtt/{auth,acl,superuser} rest on network isolation alone while the production bootstrap gate accepts MQTT_AUTH_SECRET as if it protected them
A suspended or archived tenant's edge devices still authenticate and publish: the MQTT CONNECT/ACL path resolves the tenant from the device directory and never checks the tenant's lifecycle

Concurrent device activations with one provisioning token can both succeed: activateDevice checks token_used_at in memory and its UPDATE has no token_used_at IS NULL guard, so two agents can each receive MQTT credentials

With the go-auth cache off every MQTT PUBLISH costs two database transactions on sensor-service (~7.9 ms serial, ~200 ACL checks/s ceiling per instance measured), so ACL throughput caps fleet telemetry

Directory lookup by device_code is ambiguous: device codes are unique per tenant only (registerDevice accepts operator-chosen codes) and lookupTenantId takes LIMIT 1, so a public installer/status lookup by code resolves an arbitrary tenant's device

No per-username failure limiter before async PBKDF2 on MQTT CONNECT: a flood of wrong-password CONNECTs naming a real device runs a 600k-iteration PBKDF2 per attempt and can saturate the libuv thread pool

The schema-drift validator is not expand-aware: an expand migration that relaxes NOT NULL fails the boot of the still-running previous release (entity NOT NULL over a nullable column is an error-class drift), so every nullability expand needs an entity-only release first

No writer files a water-quality measurement at a system point: water_quality_measurements.systemId exists with the one-point rule, but the entry forms' unit picker offers only tanks and water equipment, so a sump or loop sample is still filed under a unit

water_quality_parameter_configs.effectiveQuantity is kept equal to parameterQuantity(code, declaredQuantity) only by the entity's save hook: a raw-SQL or query-builder write of code or declaredQuantity, or a change to what a code means in PARAMETER_CODES, leaves the persisted quantity (and its one-active-per-quantity index) stale

A channel source's validity window (boundAt to unboundAt) does not prove its sensor stood at the point throughout: placement is decided at read time from the sensor's current location and farm's current topology, and a tank moving to another system closes nothing, so PR-4's period reads must re-derive placement for the period instead of trusting the window
A handed-over implementation PR that a person merges is not folded onto the plan ledger: the plan stays IMPLEMENTATION_REJECTED and its finding is not closed by the merge

No sensor-owned contract lets farm read a bound channel's samples over a period: request.sensor.describeChannels answers the latest sample only and channelSeries is a GraphQL read for the UI, so farm can resolve a parameter's value now but not over a period (and so cannot re-derive placement per period, FARM-MEDIUM-378)
